feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the public-sector specialization comes through well. It reads professionally and includes useful scale indicators, though it would be stronger with tighter formatting, less repetition, and more outcome-focused achievements.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative with strong career progression at NACo, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good credibility signals through concrete scope details: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms.  
- Writing is generally polished and specific, with modern, relevant expertise in Drupal, analytics, AI-enabled search, and content operations.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap heavily and dilute impact.  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity descriptions: e.g., adoption gains, efficiency improvements, engagement growth, cost savings, or campaign results.  
- Fix minor style/consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; punctuation/serial comma usage varies; “French (A2/Learning)” is awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2).” No major misspellings or grammar errors otherwise.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and repeats several themes already covered in the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the first sentence and foreground public-sector scale and leadership impact.
- Replace “building the platforms” with stronger, more executive phrasing like “leading modernization of” or “shaping.”
- Reduce the long list of functions; group related areas to improve flow and avoid sounding like a skills dump.
- Consider adding one concrete scale signal from recent roles if space allows.

Suggested rewrite:
Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Shapes enterprise digital platforms, analytics ecosystems, editorial workflows, and multimedia programs that help complex, mission-driven organizations deliver clearer, more effective user experiences, including AI-enabled discovery and content tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects.
- The long capability list duplicates the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership capabilities will make it feel more distinct and executive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and simplify wording: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership”
- Replace broad or repetitive items with sharper, higher-value terms: “AI-enabled search and content discovery” instead of “AI-enabled search and content experiences”
- Elevate operational items to leadership scope: “Workflow automation and platform integration” could become “Operational workflow automation and platform integration”
- Consider a more concise final version: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled search” repeat the header almost verbatim.
- Multimedia, advocacy, and multi-channel communications also recur in Topline Skills and multiple roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots that reinforce the CV’s themes, but the block is too dense and repeats several points already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or scope will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a simple lead-in like “Selected Recent Projects” and format each item as: project name + one concise outcome-focused line.
- Replace generic verbs (“Built,” “Developed”) with more specific ones where possible: “Launched,” “Led,” “Created,” “Produced.”
- Tighten wording for readability: e.g., “vector search and bill-level AI chat” is strong; trim extra phrases like “designed for continued campaign growth.”
- If available, add one concrete result, audience, or scale marker to 1–2 projects.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with NACo bullets in recent roles; keep this section shorter and more portfolio-style to avoid repetition.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item here; consider leading with it for variety.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical range, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo positions and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level scope, named initiatives, and outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise web strategy, campaign delivery, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for member-facing digital platforms.”
- Replace generic verbs with scoped actions: “Designed cross-channel workflows and analytics frameworks,” “built Drupal campaign microsites and modular toolkit pages,” “provided front-end/CMS troubleshooting for public-facing properties.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-led bullets; if possible add metrics such as number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, or time saved.
- Emphasize what is new since the Director role: consulting remit, AI search initiative, new campaign builds, governance modernization.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” repeats the 2022–2024 Director entry; avoid re-listing platform oversight.
- Microsites, AI search, and anniversary/campaign work also appear in Recent Projects; keep this item higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in the adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget, leading platform modernization and cross-channel communications operations.”
- Make bullets more results-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing, especially for email/social, studio build, and governance (e.g., production volume, cost savings, faster publishing, improved reporting cadence, stakeholder adoption).
- Trim tool lists in favor of business value: “Built an analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery to improve executive reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program expansion repeats earlier roles; emphasize building the in-house studio as the step-change.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and currently reads as a bridge role rather than a distinct step up. Emphasize what changed under your ownership: scale, cadence, and cross-team coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet to show ownership and impact: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the prior role and footer project; keep it here only if framed as scaling/formalizing the program.
- “publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” also appear in the Director role; avoid repeating identical governance language.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and outcomes-oriented strengths rather than broad category labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, senior-level wording: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise web and communications strategy”; “Audience-focused content planning” → “Audience-centered content operations.”
- Add one differentiator tied to recent work, e.g. “Digital governance for high-volume public-sector publishing” or “Cross-channel content systems for complex member organizations.”
- Consider a tighter version:
- Enterprise web and communications strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content planning
- If space allows, make one line more outcome-oriented: “Editorial governance and content operations at scale.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” duplicates Core Competencies: “Digital governance & editorial systems.”
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” closely repeats recent NACo role descriptions and Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. For a topline section, emphasize current strengths tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work rather than listing every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Drop lower-signal or older items unless they are job-targeted: consider removing “WordPress,” “SharePoint,” “Power Pages,” and “jQuery.”
- Replace “technical execution” phrasing with more senior language if desired: “Web Platforms & Technical Delivery” or “Web Platforms & Digital Systems.”
- If space allows, add one qualifier tied to recent impact: “enterprise Drupal platforms” or “large public-facing web properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- Platform/tool detail is already covered in Technical + IT; avoid duplicating full software inventories here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capabilities and decision impact over repeating platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools and group them: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace “SEO and performance analysis” with broader, outcome-oriented wording like “search, content and conversion performance analysis.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity • Search, content and conversion performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “Leadership reporting” also overlaps with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Make it more outcome-oriented and aligned to recent leadership-level multimedia work rather than listing production basics.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward scope and delivery: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event execution”
- If space allows, add scale/impact language tied to recent roles: “Built and operated in-house broadcast studio supporting advocacy programming, recurring video content and live events”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production”
- Keep terms parallel and concise; avoid mixing tools, formats, and functions inconsistently

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies
- Tool-level detail like PTZ systems may fit better under Technical + IT unless this section is meant to signal specialization

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a bare inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since Drupal is the strongest and most recent platform in the experience section, this item should emphasize depth/order rather than repeat generic CMS names.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider leading with depth: “Drupal (enterprise migration, modular builds) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If formatting allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Keep this item platform-focused only; avoid adding “CMS modernization” here since that already appears elsewhere.
- If space is tight, consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it is used meaningfully in recent work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.”
- Drupal/modernization strength is already evidenced in recent NACo roles, so avoid repeating broad platform claims without context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required by the role; they add little value at senior level.
- Consider replacing “jQuery” with “JavaScript/jQuery” only if it reflects current use; otherwise remove to avoid dating the profile.
- If space allows, add a brief qualifier tied to impact, e.g., “for Drupal builds, campaign microsites, analytics instrumentation, and workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” “Workflow automation”). Keep the stronger version in one place.
- “GitHub Actions” may also overlap conceptually with “Automation & Workflow Systems”; keep it here only if you want to signal developer-facing CI/CD capability.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too list-heavy and mixes automation platforms with project/collaboration tools. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and tighten naming: “Automation & Workflow: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier” and move “Jira, Asana, Basecamp, Trello” to a separate “Project Management Tools” line if space allows.
- Keep only tools you’ve actively used in recent roles; prioritize Airtable and Power Automate if they supported NACo workflow/governance improvements.
- Standardize labels: use “Microsoft Teams” instead of “Teams”; consider dropping Slack if it was only a communication channel, not a workflow system.
- If you want more impact, add a brief qualifier elsewhere, e.g., “Built editorial and reporting workflows in Airtable and Power Automate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies.
- Slack and Teams read as collaboration tools, not strong differentiators for a senior digital leader.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a generic tool list and misses the scale/context already established in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise email operations and member engagement without repeating newsletter details from work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize platform names: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show level of use, e.g. **Enterprise campaign automation, newsletter operations, and member communications**
- Consider a fuller rewrite: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | Email campaign delivery, audience segmentation, and member engagement operations**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already covered well in recent work experience.
- Don’t repeat broad “multi-channel communications” language already captured in Core Competencies.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, it should emphasize methods and business use, not repeat the same product list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics & Optimization Tools**
- Tighten and sharpen the list: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI dashboarding**
- If space allows, add one impact cue instead of pure tools: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • KPI dashboarding • SEO analysis • experimentation**
- Consider dropping the weakest/generic term (“Dashboarding”) unless reframed as **KPI dashboarding** or **executive reporting**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; keep one version tool-focused and the other outcome-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating all five elsewhere unless this section is meant purely for ATS.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any available outputs.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted through two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function…”
- Add concrete outputs if known: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence of video updates, audience growth, or process improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce broad channel lists; focus on 2–3 strongest contributions.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day workflows for web, email, social and multimedia production. Provided informal supervision and task direction for a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- Workflow/governance language also appears in later roles; keep this entry more executional and foundational.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital content and multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the policy/research support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and strongest proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Trim vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a more specific support verb, e.g., “produced supporting digital and multimedia content for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope: number of episodes launched, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or whether the podcast became a recurring series.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing general multimedia production; later roles already cover video, digital content and channel operations more strongly.
- Don’t repeat “first” language too often across NACo entries unless each launch is clearly distinct.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with stronger, more strategic multimedia claims elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, and keep production capabilities at a higher-level skills or experience level.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a cleaner tools list: **Adobe Creative Cloud: Premiere Pro, Audition, Photoshop, Illustrator**
- Replace broad workflow phrases with more specific technical capabilities if true: **video editing, audio post-production, graphic asset creation**
